item.title: Async Programming Is Just Inject Time
item.description:
📝 The compiler knows what the instruction address is—it’s the one that puts it there—and so for each function call site, that’s just a static piece of information that gets passed in. toString(); The toString method that gets called depends on the type of the receiver object. This isn’t determined at compile time, but instead a lookup that happens at runtime.
🔗 Read more: https://willhbr.net/2026/03/02/async-inject-and-effects/

item.title: First MacBook Neo Benchmarks Are In
item.description:
📝 The ‌MacBook Neo‌ earned a single-core score of 3461 and a multi-core score of 8668, along with a Metal score of 31286. Here's how the Neo's scores compare to ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro and other devices that make apt comparisons: iPhone 16 Pro - 3445 single-core, 8624 multi-core, 32575 Metal M1 MacBook Air - 2346 single-core, 8342 multi-core, 33148 Metal M4 MacBook Air - 3696 single-core, 14730 multi-core, 54630 Metal M3 iPad Air - 3048 single-core, 11678 multi-core, 44395 Metal iPad 11 - 2587 single-core, 6036 multi-core, 19395 Metal Since the ‌MacBook Neo‌ has one fewer GPU core than the ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro, it makes sense to see a slightly lower Metal score. Apple does not compare ‌MacBook Neo‌ performance to other Macs, iPads, or iPhones.
🔗 Read more: https://www.macrumors.com/2026/03/05/macbook-neo-first-benchmarks/
